conflicts.point: Whether pre-market approval standards and static review boards are necessary to prevent irreversible harm, or whether they impose lethal operational delays that exceed software error risks.

positions.stance: Static pre-market approval boards impose lethal delays by trapping life-saving tools in regulatory review, making the status quo baseline of human bias and delay more dangerous than iterative software errors.
Permanent state injuries like wrongful incarceration or delayed critical care require strict pre-market safety barriers and human vetoes because post-hoc measures cannot undo irreversible harm.

conflicts.point: Whether real-time telemetry and market-driven oversight can effectively catch and correct algorithmic errors faster than pre-deployment regulatory review.

positions.stance: Real-time monitoring and competitive market dynamics catch and correct local software errors faster than static pre-deployment review boards.
Live telemetry is insufficient because early errors compound invisibly in black-box models, and post-deployment corrections arrive too late after harm has occurred.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-market approval standards and static review boards are necessary to prevent irreversible harm, or whether they impose lethal operational delays that exceed software error risks.
verdicts.rationale: Both positions track genuine risks: accelerationists document real clinical wait-time reductions of 15 to 40 percent, while safetyists emphasize that post-hoc corrections cannot undo wrongful incarceration or delayed critical care. Neither side definitively proves that its preferred baseline—manual error versus software error—inflicts lower total harm across healthcare and criminal justice.

verdicts.conflict: Whether real-time telemetry and market-driven oversight can effectively catch and correct algorithmic errors faster than pre-deployment regulatory review.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position is stronger because vendor trade-secret claims and licensing restrictions currently block independent external verification of model weights. Accelerationists assert that market dynamics correct errors quickly, but they offer no mechanism to bypass proprietary secrecy barriers that prevent live telemetry from being audited.
